title: Challenge of the Yukon
paragraphs: Northern adventure centered on Royal Canadian Mounted Police Sergeant William Preston and his dog Yukon King. The program began as a WXYZ regional serial/adventure, expanded to ABC in 1947, moved to Mutual in 1950, and was renamed Sergeant Preston of the Yukon in November 1951.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: WXYZ local/regional era (February 3, 1938 to May 28, 1947) on [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]], ABC network era (June 12, 1947 to December 30, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], Mutual Challenge of the Yukon era (January 2, 1950 to November 11, 1951) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and Mutual Sergeant Preston era (November 13, 1951 to 1954) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Jay Michael (announcer and performer), Paul Sutton (performer), George W. Trendle (producer, creator, and performer), Fred Flowerday (director and performer), Fran Striker (editor, writer, and performer), Charles D. Livingstone (performer, director, and editor), and Mildred Merrill (writer and announcer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], [[org|org.a0d8a72797b5185f|WXYZ]], [[org|org.4873e07a843601f0|Michigan Radio Network]], and [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].
The stories often return to Murder and violent crime, Gold mining and prospecting, Working dogs, Robbery and theft, Royal Canadian Mounted Police / Mounties, and Mining claims and property disputes.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Mountie and northern-frontier adventure in American popular radio, Breakfast-cereal sponsorship and youth premiums, and Sergeant Preston across the radio-to-television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-lone-ranger|The Lone Ranger]], [[show|the-green-hornet|The Green Hornet]], [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]], and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]].
